Duration Factory API Reference¶

Back to PlussQit API Reference

The free functions in pluss::duration construct and render elapsed-time arrays. They are separate from the Duration method reference: factories answer how a value enters the type; methods answer what an existing Duration can do.

Choose By Intent¶

  • Use nanos, microseconds, milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours, days, or weeks when the source unit is known at the call site.

  • Use make(values, Unit) when the unit is selected at runtime. pluss::make_duration(...) is its intentional root-level forwarding form.

  • Use range for an inclusive, fixed-width one-dimensional progression.

  • Use zeros and full for shape-first allocation; use their _like counterparts when an existing Duration supplies the shape.

  • Use random for seeded or entropy-seeded uniform integer nanoseconds in a half-open interval.

  • Use print for diagnostic rendering to a string or stream.

All duration values are stored as signed 64-bit nanoseconds. Construction is exact: integer inputs never pass through floating point. Public arrays support ranks zero through three; explicit shapes reject negative extents, cardinality overflow, and flat-data length mismatches before allocating. Unit scaling also checks signed-nanosecond overflow. Duration::kNaT is the reserved absent value.

The unit constructors accept four data geometries: one integer produces a scalar; a contiguous integer range or flat braced list produces rank one; rectangular nested braces infer rank and shape; and (flat, sizes) applies runtime shape metadata. Every deterministic output in this family comes from examples/CodeH/duration_factory_reference_demo.cpp; its transcript is docs/sphinx/_verified/duration_factory_reference_output.txt.
